messages:
incident-bot: PAGED: P1 - TP4 multi-GPU collective degradations observed across a subset of nodes. Pager -> @sre-oncall
sre-oncall: Acknowledged. What symptoms are we seeing? Any customer impact yet?
maria.chen: Runtime shows repeated `NCCL: UNRECOVERABLE` and `rendezvous timeout` entries from pods on gpunode-17..19. Several TP4 training shards stuck, kube shows pods in `ContainerCreating` then `CrashLoopBackOff`.
devin.patel: Metrics correlate: NCCL error spikes at 12:14 UTC, request latency p99 doubled, throughput down ~65% for tp4-multi pool. Affected workloads include two customer training clusters and three internal eval runners.
nashwin: Extract from runtime log (one representative pod):
```
E [12:14:22] nccl_comm.c:456 NCCL ERROR: UNRECOVERABLE - internal error
E [12:14:22] cuda.cu:198 CUDA_ERROR_LAUNCH_FAILED
W rendezvous: kv mismatch, wait timed out after 120s
```
ops-bridge: Ops bridge created -> https://meet.link/ops-1795554321 (join for live troubleshooting)
eng-runtime: Noted recent driver rollout `gpu-driver-5.2.1` to tp4 pool last night. Could be a regression interacting with NCCL/Xid handling.
sre-oncall: Immediate actions: (1) isolate suspect nodes, (2) route new work to fallback pool variants, (3) collect NVML traces and core dumps.
maria.chen: Isolating nodes now: `kubectl label node gpunode-17 isolated=nccl-incident` (applied to 17-19). Scheduler eviction in progress.
devin.patel: Initiating routing change: `redwoodctl route set --pool tp4-quant-fallback --selector shard_group=tp4 --drain 300s`. Will monitor errors during cutover.
customer-success: Notifying impacted customers: "We're investigating multi-GPU comm failures affecting your training shards. Failover to a fallback pool is in progress; some restarts expected. ETA 20-40m." :loudspeaker:
eng-runtime: NVML dmon from gpunode-17 shows ECC counters rising and repeated Xid 79 reports. `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=err_detected --format=csv` shows errors on GPU1.
nashwin: In previous infra tests, Xid 79 often corresponded to driver-side hangs; restarting `nvidia-persistenced` occasionally helps but isn't a solid fix mid-training.
sre-oncall: Plan: cordon+drain isolated nodes, scale up fallback pool by +3 nodes, apply temporary runtime policy to prefer single-GPU quantized variants.
ops-bridge: Autoscaler triggered: scaling `tp4-quant-fallback` up by 3 nodes (request sent), ETA ~90s.
maria.chen: Evictions happening; one customer job failed over and resumed on fallback (with lower throughput). Two customer-facing endpoints returned intermittent 503s during the switch.
devin.patel: Collected dmesg and core dumps from gpunode-18. Excerpt:
```
[1234.567] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, PID 24155
[1234.568] kernel: task hung in schedule(), resetting
```
eng-runtime: Spinning a canary: rolling back driver on a single node to `gpu-driver-5.1.8` and running representative TP4 job. Monitoring 5m.
incident-bot: Canary started at 12:28 UTC.
sre-oncall: Capture artifacts: full NCCL debug traces, /var/log/nvidia-installer.log, driver package hashes, kube evict logs, and routing decisions.
eng-runtime: Canary job finished 1 epoch w/o NCCL errors (monitor window 5m). No regression so far.
maria.chen: Proceeding with staged rollback to 5.1.8 across remaining nodes that are not quarantined. Keeping isolated nodes labeled until health verified.
customer-success: Sent customer X update: "Driver rollback and failover underway, some jobs delayed. We'll provide incident report after RCA."
nashwin: Post-incident checklist: map rollout timeline vs error onset, check firmware/BIOS updates, compare CUDA/NVML versions, validate kernel oops, test NVLINK topology, and reproduce at low scale.
sre-oncall: Current status at 12:47 UTC: Failover largely successful, most traffic on fallback, 3 nodes quarantined, driver rollback in progress. Impact: brief 503s, one priority training job ~25m delay. Escalation level lowered P1->P2; continue monitoring 4h.
eng-runtime: Creating follow-up ticket INF-3921 with stored artifacts and timeline for deeper triage (driver vs hardware).
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE posted at 12:47 UTC - mitigation applied, tracking follow-ups."
